Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) is a well-established cardiothoracic surgical procedure performed to restore adequate blood flow to the heart when the coronary arteries become blocked or severely narrowed. These blockages, most often caused by coronary artery disease, reduce the supply of oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle and can lead to symptoms such as chest pain, breathlessness, fatigue, or an increased risk of heart attack. 

During CABG surgery, a healthy blood vessel is taken from another part of the body—commonly the chest, leg, or arm—and grafted onto the affected coronary artery. This new vessel creates an alternate route for blood to bypass the blockage and reach the heart muscle effectively. Depending on the patient’s condition and the extent of disease, the procedure may be performed on a beating or temporarily stopped heart and may involve multiple bypass grafts to address widespread arterial involvement. The surgery is carried out under general anaesthesia and typically lasts several hours, with every step planned carefully to ensure precision and safety. 

CABG is usually recommended for patients with advanced coronary artery disease, especially when multiple arteries are involved or when symptoms persist despite medication or less invasive treatments. The procedure has been shown to significantly improve heart function, relieve symptoms, reduce the risk of future cardiac events, and enhance overall quality of life.

Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) – A Modern Heart Care Solution

TAVI is an advanced, minimally invasive procedure used to treat aortic valve stenosis—a condition where the heart valve becomes stiff and restricts blood flow. This can lead to symptoms like breathlessness, fatigue, dizziness, or fainting, especially in older adults.

Unlike traditional open-heart surgery, TAVI does not require opening the chest. A new valve is delivered through a thin catheter, usually inserted via an artery in the leg, and placed inside the damaged valve. The new valve starts working immediately, improving blood flow.

Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) is an advanced, minimally invasive procedure used to treat aortic valve stenosis, a condition where the heart valve becomes narrowed and restricts blood flow. This condition may cause symptoms such as breathlessness, fatigue, dizziness, or fainting, especially in older adults.

During the TAVI procedure, a new valve is carefully delivered to the heart through a thin catheter, usually inserted through an artery in the leg. The new valve is placed inside the damaged valve, where it expands and immediately begins functioning. Because the chest is not opened and the heart continues beating during the procedure, TAVI offers a safer alternative to traditional open-heart surgery for many patients. 🫀

This treatment is often recommended for elderly individuals or patients who may be at higher risk for conventional surgery. Recovery is typically faster, with less discomfort and a shorter hospital stay. Many patients experience noticeable improvement in breathing, energy levels, and daily activities soon after the procedure.

Stay safe by drinking enough water, replenishing electrolytes, covering up, staying in shaded areas, and avoiding going out during peak heat hours whenever possible.

Hypertension is often called the “silent killer” for a reason. It may not show visible symptoms, yet it can quietly impact your heart, brain, and kidneys over time.

Don’t wait for warning signs to take charge of your health. Monitor your blood pressure regularly, stay physically active, maintain a balanced diet, prioritise quality sleep, and manage stress effectively.
Small lifestyle changes today can make a lasting difference to your health tomorrow.
